trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out down, up or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down.
I can't rule out right, left or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.
Going right, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 3; going down, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 3. So the line goes up.
Going up leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.

Going to number 4 would leave both cell (1,5) and cell (1,7) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going down would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes right.
The line must go up: down is number 16, which comes later.
Going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Cell (1,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (2,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going left would force the line onto number 12 before its turn. So the line goes down.
The line must go right: left is number 11, which comes later; down is number 9, which comes later.
Going down, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,6). So the line goes right.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down.
Going left, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,6). So the line goes down.
Going down would cut off the bottom-right corner (10 cells); going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Cell (5,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,2). So the line goes down.
Going down would cut off the bottom-left corner (10 cells). So the line goes left.
Going down would leave both cell (7,1) and cell (7,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going left would cut off the left side (6 cells). So the line goes up.
Number 11 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (3,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going up would strand number 14: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Cell (6,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Cell (5,7) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
